key_insight: ARISE turns medical image understanding into a transparent 5-step agentic workflow that uses image-grounded self-evaluation to improve interpretability and reduce hallucination in IBD assessment.
clinical_relevance: The framework may help clinicians get more reliable, explainable support for reviewing wireless capsule endoscopy and intestinal ultrasound in Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis.
method: Generates an initial hypothesis from the image.
Summarizes image-grounded evidence and refines the answer using that evidence.
Performs symbolic verification before producing the final diagnosis.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on two independent patient cohorts—wireless capsule endoscopy images for Crohn’s disease and B-mode ultrasound data for ulcerative colitis—with consistent gains over baseline VLMs.
watch_item: Performance and interpretability depend on high-quality image evidence and robust validation, so real-world deployment still needs careful testing for failure modes and generalization.
paper_title: ARISE: Adaptive Agentic Reasoning with Image-grounded Self-Evaluation for Interpretable IBD Assessment
